chronology: RECAP: The Metabaron destroys the Metabunker; Tonto and Lothar strand on a primitive muddy world, begin rebuilding while narrating Metabaron history.

RECAP: Don Nicanor's Philodendran forces breach the barricade sheltering Melmoth and Dona Vicenta; he fails to recognize her as his daughter; she sacrifices her fingernails; he grants permission for her marriage to Melmoth.

RECAP: Melmoth is horrified by Dona Vicenta's cybernetic eyes; his psyche fractures into Steelhead (warrior) and Zaran (poet). A TechnoCardinal demands the Philodendran people vacate for Bikramen mining; Don Nicanor refuses and bombardment begins. Dona Vicenta begs Steelhead to fight; Steelhead kills himself to silence Zaran.

Castle under bombardment: Melmoth/Steelhead declares the poet persona dead. Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha is killed. A young companion with mechanical eyes selects a cybernetic replacement head with 360-degree multi-ocular vision.
Melmoth/Steelhead in a black aircraft destroys seven fossil-like targets and the family castle; the young mechanical-eyed passenger mourns but is ordered to focus on battle.
Surviving petro-morphs transform into space battleships and launch as a massive swarm while the two masters argue tactics.

Space battle: petro-morphs merge into a gigantic combined vessel. The Metabaron orders Metacraft to execute an immediate about-turn, exploiting superior maneuverability to buy time against the enormous enemy ship.
Atomic maxi-okos weapon destroys the floating mothership-flagship identified as the Maleroute tree, causing dependent masses to collapse. A woman blames a metal-head companion for the destruction.

Metacraft leaps thousands of light years through inter-space and lands before the sealed doors of Amalek XII's techno-temple on the Techno Central Planet. Temple guards attempt capture rather than vaporization.
Heavy cyborg warrior and Milady exit the craft; a spherical energy field kills technopapal guardians en masse; the pair advance toward the temple.
The armored figure fights through an interior chamber, fires energy into a golden organic structure, expels a small figure through a vertical shaft, and crashes through a crystalline barrier.
The party reaches a circular doorway and demands audience with Aghlex/Amalek XII; a guard deploys a giant technoscarab; the champion refuses to retreat.
The technoscarab is destroyed; Amalek XII is summoned under threat of total destruction.
The Supreme Metabaron activates a pan-atomic anti-shield; technomonk faction attempts coercion and kidnapping; a blast disperses them; their leader capitulates.

Steelhead abducts Amalek XII. Philodendra placed under siege by thousands of technodestroyers. A technopope secured in ruins of the presidential palace on Philodendra. Speakers debate Amalek succession (XIII, XIV, XV).

Plan Item 3: private meeting with Dona Vicenta Gabriela de Rokha, acting president of the Troglosocialik Federation; she overcomes grief and agrees to the plan. Plan Item 4: Bikramen presence in the Troglosocialik system announced galaxy-wide.
News of Bikramen triggers a chain of military encirclements in space: Empire warships surround technodestroyers; Magnate union surrounds them; pirate fleets wait at the edges.

Dona Vicenta negotiates a joint Bikramen governance contract with the Empire, Magnate, and Techno Guild; displaced populations promised profit shares and artificial replacement planets. Allied armadas purge pirates from trade routes. Philodendra's population evacuates to Magna; Dona Vicenta watches from the ruins of her castle, now her father's tomb.
Mass exodus from Philodendra in ordered silence; dead buried with Philodendra soil per funerary custom; planet left to industrial devastation.
Dona Vicenta, in an artificial environment, reveals her pregnancy; metallic/cybernetic man claims Castaka dynastic succession; she denies emotional paternity, saying her love belonged to another man.
Dona Vicenta contracts paleo-tuberculosis; the master brings her to the Metabunker for emergency treatment; General Zoththo assumes the presidency; medical examination reveals twins.

In a mechanical birthing chamber: one boy (Castaka heir) and one girl (linked to poet-lover and Krleza); mother too weak to deliver both. The masked female master is asked to choose which twin to save. Volume ends unresolved.

Tonto and Lothar discuss why Steelhead saved a daughter rather than eliminating all witnesses; confirm Steelhead had only one child, a girl; question of how the Castaka line survived is deferred to the next episode.
locations: Philodendra / Philoendra — Troglosocialik Federation homeworld; site of castle siege, mass exodus, Dona Vicenta's father's tomb, and the ruins of the presidential palace; abandoned to industrial exploitation after evacuation.
Techno Central Planet — seat of Amalek XII's power; home to his sealed techno-temple defended by technopapal guardians, a technoscarab, and layered automated defenses.
The Metabunker — mobile or fixed installation rebuilt by Tonto and Lothar; used as emergency medical facility for Dona Vicenta.
Space battle zone — open space site of petro-morph transformation, the Metacraft about-turn, and the atomic maxi-okos strike on the Maleroute tree flagship.
Artificial city environment (unnamed) — synthetic habitat where Dona Vicenta lives post-evacuation, with artificial air, rain, plastic vegetation, and holographic birds.
Magna — destination for Philodendran emigrants departing aboard Techno-Techno transports.
Troglosocialik system — political and spatial context for the Bikramen announcement and multi-faction convergence.
Ruined industrial wasteland (Tonto and Lothar's location) — open landscape with a colossal latticework face-shaped structure; site of the frame narrative.
lore_laws: Petro-morphs are shape-shifting entities that can transform into space battleships and merge individually into a single gigantic combined vessel.
Inter-space travel uses anti-matter propulsion enabling jumps of thousands of light years in seconds.
The Castaka bloodline is said to sire only male children, making twin girls a lineage-disrupting anomaly.
Metacraft is a voice-interfaced craft that confirms spoken commands and carries a multi-layer protective shield strong enough to withstand a techno-temple's defense systems.
Advanced medicine — metasurgery, mega-antibiotics, holographic ultrasound — exists but cannot cure paleo-tuberculosis, an ancient disease still lethal despite futuristic treatment.
The Techno-Technos mine a rare mineral called Bikramen; a TechnoCardinal acts as their official representative when issuing planetary ultimatums.
A pan-atomic anti-shield and an escalated mode called mega-mortis exist as defensive/offensive technologies available to the Metabaron.
Artificial planets can be constructed and offered as compensatory replacements for displaced populations.
Tonto and Lothar are bound by laws of robotics compelling service to their master regardless of circumstance.
Amalek XII holds the title Supreme Technopope; the Technoguild maintains a numbered succession (XIII, XIV, XV) prepared to replace him.
major_events: Melmoth/Steelhead eliminates the Zaran poet persona and destroys the family castle, killing Don Nicanor Rosamel de Rokha.
Petro-morphs transform into space battleships and merge into a single gigantic combined vessel, escalating from ground-level threat to full galactic menace.
The Metabaron executes a precision about-turn maneuver with Metacraft to outpace the merged petro-morph ship through maneuverability rather than firepower.
The atomic maxi-okos weapon destroys the Maleroute tree flagship, ending the central space battle against the enemy mothership.
Metacraft breaches Amalek XII's sealed techno-temple and the party fights through technopapal guardians and a technoscarab to reach the inner sanctum.
Steelhead abducts Amalek XII, triggering Technoguild succession crisis and placing Philodendra under siege by thousands of technodestroyers.
Galaxy-wide announcement of Bikramen in the Troglosocialik system draws every major faction into simultaneous confrontation.
Empire, Magnate, and Techno Guild sign a joint Bikramen contract; allied armadas purge pirates; entire population of Philodendra evacuated to Magna and planet abandoned to industrial exploitation.
Dona Vicenta contracts fatal paleo-tuberculosis; twin pregnancy discovered; forced medical choice between Castaka male heir and a girl linked to her poet-lover is left unresolved at volume end.
open_uncertainties: How the Castaka/Metabaron patrilineal line survived if Steelhead fathered only a daughter — explicitly deferred to the next episode.
Whether 'Aghlex XII' (p11) and 'Amalek XII' elsewhere refer to the same character or represent a transcription error.
The exact identity of the young passenger with mechanical eyes traveling with Melmoth/Steelhead — possibly Dona Vicenta or a separate character.
Whether the armored cyborg leading the temple assault is definitively the same individual as Steelhead, or a distinct current Metabaron figure.
The exact nature of the Maleroute tree — whether it is a ship, a megastructure, or an organic installation.
The identity of the 'metal-head' companion blamed by the woman for failing to prevent the Maleroute tree's destruction.
Whether Krleza is a person, a place, or a clan, and its precise relationship to the girl twin and the man Dona Vicenta loves.
The identity of the masked female master who must choose between the two twins on p23 — possibly Milady or a distinct character.
Whether the forced twin choice is resolved in this volume or carried into the next episode; the final page leaves it unresolved.
The exact mechanism of the spherical defensive energy field used by the cyborg warrior — not named or technically explained on any page.
recurring_motifs: Duality and split identity: Steelhead versus Zaran within Melmoth; bodily versus spiritual paternity in Dona Vicenta's pregnancy; warrior pragmatism versus poetic idealism throughout.

Cybernetic sacrifice and bodily transformation: Dona Vicenta's fingernails and eyes; Melmoth's cyborg body; interchangeable cybernetic heads; metallic man's steel skull against his claimed human heart.
Dynastic succession under threat: the Castaka bloodline, forced twin selection, Amalek XII's numbered succession (XIII-XV), and the unresolved question of how the Metabaron line survived.
Resource extraction as the engine of galactic conflict: Bikramen drives every faction — Techno-Technos, Empire, Magnate, pirates — into collision.
Small defeating large through cunning: Metacraft's about-turn against the merged petro-morph ship; Steelhead's multi-step political plan outmaneuvering galaxy-spanning powers.
Tonto and Lothar as frame narrators: stranded after Metabunker destruction, they recount Metabaron history and bind present action to dynastic memory.
Displacement and mourning for a destroyed homeworld: Philodendra's evacuation, funerary soil customs, and Dona Vicenta's attachment to her ruined castle and father's tomb.
title: Galactic Threat
